model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between coverage and the number of completions (k) for four different Llama model configurations: Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. The x-axis, labeled “Number of completions (k),” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 2⁰ (1) to 2⁸ (256), with tick marks at each power of two. The y-axis, labeled “Coverage,” uses a linear scale ranging from 0.2 to 0.9, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The Llama-3B line (solid blue with circle markers) starts at approximately 0.43 at k=1 and rises steadily to about 0.88 at k=256. The Llama-3B + FT line (dashed green with triangle markers) begins at approximately 0.44 and increases to roughly 0.89. The Llama-1B line (solid light blue with square markers) starts at about 0.28 and climbs to approximately 0.84. The Llama-1B + FT line (dashed light green with diamond markers) begins at around 0.29 and reaches about 0.83. All lines show a consistent upward trend, with coverage increasing as the number of completions grows, and the fine-tuned versions (FT) generally achieving slightly higher coverage than their base counterparts across the range.
